ground_truth.description: PriceAware.getCurrentPriceInPeg() allows callers to request a current-block price. When forceCurBlock is true and the update window has elapsed, the function obtains a Uniswap-style AMM quote and can update the cached token price from that quote. Because the quote is computed from current pair reserves, a flash loan can temporarily distort the reserves and cause the protocol to use a manipulated price.
ground_truth.impact: Wrong prices break the core functionality of the contracts such as borrowing on margin, liquidations, etc.
ground_truth.mitigation: Do not use the current Uniswap spot quote as the token price. Use a TWAP oracle based on Uniswap cumulative price variables.
ground_truth.title: [H-03] Price feed can be manipulated

ground_truth.description: Synth.realise() calculates baseValueLP with Utils.calcLiquidityHoldings() from the pool's current baseAmount/tokenAmount reserves and total LP supply, and calculates baseValueSynth with Utils.calcActualSynthUnits() using the same current reserve ratio. If the manipulated values make the LP holdings appear to exceed the synth value, realise() treats the difference as a premium and burns LP tokens from the pool. A flash loan or a large LP holder can shift the AMM ratio before calling realise(), then shift it back and repeat the operation.
ground_truth.impact: An attacker can use transient AMM-ratio manipulation to cause LP tokens held by Synth to be burned, then redeem their own LP tokens for a larger share of the pool's underlying assets, extracting value from other pool LP holders.
ground_truth.mitigation: Do not value LP tokens with the instantaneous AMM spot price. Use a manipulation-resistant TWAP or Chainlink oracle for token pricing, or use an anti-flash-loan LP valuation formula such as Alpha Finance's fair-LP formula.
ground_truth.title: [H-05] Synth realise is vulnerable to flash loan attacks

ground_truth.description: SynthVault._deposit() converts the deposited synth amount into BASE weight using Utils.calcSpotValueInBase(), which ultimately computes amount * pool.baseAmount() / pool.tokenAmount() from current AMM reserves. The resulting weight is stored and later used by calcReward() to allocate an unrelated BASE reward reserve. An attacker can temporarily increase the BASE-per-token spot price, deposit synth while the price is distorted, and then restore the pool; the inflated stored weight remains after the manipulation ends.
ground_truth.impact: The attacker can inflate their stored SynthVault weight relative to the deposited synth amount and claim a large share of BASE-funded rewards. The cost of manipulation depends on pool liquidity and the potential profit depends on the reward reserve, so the attack can be profitable under certain circumstances.
ground_truth.mitigation: Track a TWAP price of the synth, store deposited synth amounts, and calculate user and total weight on the fly from the TWAP multiplied by the deposit amount instead of at deposit time.
ground_truth.title: [H-06] SynthVault rewards can be gamed

predictions.description: Several Router paths transfer the entire current Router balance instead of only the assets produced by the current operation. In removeLiquidityExact for BNB, removeLiquiditySingle, and swapAssetToSynth, pre-existing BASE/WBNB balances can be included in the caller's output or used to mint synths. Any user able to execute the relevant path, such as an LP holder, can exploit assets accidentally sent to the Router, residual dust, or balances left by another operation.
predictions.impact: Attackers can appropriate unrelated BASE/WBNB held by Router or mint synths against those funds, causing direct loss of protocol or user assets.
predictions.mitigation: Record each relevant Router asset balance before the operation and transfer only the post-operation balance delta. Avoid retaining user funds in Router; add explicit sweeping controls for any pre-existing balances and validate all intermediate transfer amounts.
predictions.title: Router balance sweeping allows liquidity withdrawers to steal unrelated assets

predictions.description: addDividend computes dailyAllocation using maxTrades but does not track or enforce the maximum number of dividend events per era, and the shown Router state includes no effective per-era payout counter or reset in this path. A caller can repeatedly trade against a curated pool while emissions are enabled and trigger repeated Reserve grants, allowing the reserve allocation intended for a bounded number of trades to be paid out repeatedly.
predictions.impact: The Reserve can be drained faster than intended, transferring protocol incentives to the curated pool and its LP holders and reducing funds available for other protocol obligations.
predictions.mitigation: Track dividend events and cumulative dividend allocation per era, reset the counters at an explicit era boundary, and reject or cap payouts once maxTrades or the configured aggregate allocation is reached. Enforce the cap in the Reserve as a defense in depth.
predictions.title: Curated-pool dividend payouts are unlimited despite maxTrades configuration

predictions.description: _handleTransferIn calls transferFrom or WBNB transfer without checking the returned boolean, and its computed actual amount is not used by the public liquidity and swap entrypoints. _handleTransferOut likewise ignores the return value of ERC20 transfer. For tokens that return false or otherwise do not transfer the requested amount, Router can continue into Pool accounting as though the operation succeeded, while users may receive no output or LP/swap accounting may become inconsistent.
predictions.impact: Users can lose input assets without receiving the expected LP tokens or swap output, and pools can become misaccounted or unusable for affected assets.
predictions.mitigation: Use SafeERC20-style wrappers that revert on false or malformed return data, measure pre/post balances for every input, and pass the actual received amount into Pool operations. Verify output transfer success before finalizing accounting.
predictions.title: Router ignores token transfer return values and received amounts in asset ingress and egress

predictions.description: claimForMember subtracts _claimable from bondedLP and then checks whether _claimable equals the post-claim bondedLP. When a claim occurs at exactly half of the remaining vesting amount, the comparison succeeds even though LP remains, causing claimRate to be set to zero. The remaining LP can no longer vest unless another deposit resets the rate or DAO release is invoked.
predictions.impact: Members can have part of their bonded LP permanently locked, resulting in loss or indefinite denial of access to redeemable liquidity.
predictions.mitigation: Capture the pre-claim bonded balance, determine whether _claimable equals that pre-claim balance, and set claimRate to zero only when the post-claim bondedLP is zero. Add tests for claims at zero, half, and full vesting.
predictions.title: BondVault claim logic can permanently lock half of a member’s remaining LP

predictions.description: depositForMember computes claimRate using integer division of bondedLP by bondingPeriodSeconds. Any deposit smaller than the vesting period, and any residual amount below that period after claims, receives a zero claim rate. calcBondedLP then returns zero indefinitely because elapsed time multiplied by the zero rate is zero.
predictions.impact: Bonded LP amounts can remain trapped in BondVault indefinitely, requiring administrative release or another deposit to recover them.
predictions.mitigation: Track vesting using a numerator and denominator or an accrued remainder so fractional per-second entitlement is preserved. Alternatively provide a clearly defined final-dust claim path that does not depend on bondRelease.
predictions.title: Integer truncation can create permanently unclaimable BondVault dust

predictions.description: harvestSingle credits newly minted synths to mapMemberSynth_deposit but never updates mapMember_depositTime. Since withdraw checks only the older global deposit timestamp, a member can harvest newly accrued rewards and immediately withdraw them without waiting minimumDepositTime.
predictions.impact: Users can immediately exit with freshly harvested rewards, defeating the intended one-hour lock and enabling short-term or mercenary participation that the lock was intended to prevent.
predictions.mitigation: Apply the intended lock to harvested rewards by updating the applicable member or member-and-synth withdrawal timestamp when harvestSingle credits synthReward, or track deposit timestamps per balance tranche and enforce the lock against each tranche.
predictions.title: Harvested Synth rewards bypass the minimum withdrawal lock

predictions.description: harvestAll iterates over the entire stakedSynthAssets array on every call. The array permanently grows whenever a new synth is first deposited and entries are never removed, while each eligible entry performs reward calculation and may invoke reserve and pool contracts.
predictions.impact: HarvestAll can revert due to gas exhaustion, leaving users unable to claim rewards through the aggregate function and imposing increasingly high gas costs as historical synth assets accumulate.
predictions.mitigation: Provide paginated harvesting with start and end indexes, or let users harvest only explicitly selected synths. Do not require iterating over the full historical stakedSynthAssets array in one transaction.
predictions.title: SynthVault harvestAll becomes increasingly gas-heavy and can become unusable

predictions.description: withdraw and _processWithdraw accept arbitrary basisPoints without requiring a value between 0 and 10000. Values above 10000 can produce a calculated amount greater than the recorded balance and cause subtraction underflow, while values that round one component to zero can remove deposit principal without proportionally removing its recorded weight.
predictions.impact: Malformed requests can reliably revert, and rounding mismatches can let a member retain reward weight after reducing deposited synth principal, potentially receiving excess emissions relative to remaining capital.
predictions.mitigation: Require basisPoints <= 10000 and reject zero or otherwise ineffective withdrawals where appropriate. Calculate a single proportional share and ensure principal and weight reductions cannot diverge materially due to rounding; clear residual weight when the corresponding deposit reaches zero.
predictions.title: Withdrawal basis points are not range-validated, enabling caller-triggered reverts and inconsistent partial accounting

predictions.description: depositForMember is public, accepts any member address, and does not require amount > 0. A caller can invoke it with a valid synth, a victim address, and zero amount; transferFrom of zero succeeds, while _deposit still resets the victim’s global and per-synth lock timestamps.
predictions.impact: An attacker can repeatedly reset a victim’s one-hour withdrawal and harvest lock at negligible cost, preventing the victim from withdrawing or harvesting their SynthVault position for as long as the attacker continues the calls.
predictions.mitigation: Add require(amount > 0), validate that the transferred amount is positive, and use an authorization model for deposits on behalf of another member or require explicit member consent.
predictions.title: Arbitrary zero-value deposits can repeatedly lock another user’s SynthVault position

ground_truth.description: AssetHandler.getLiquidityTokenValue() loads the current market and values a liquidity token from its proportional asset-cash and fCash claims. getCashClaims() and getHaircutCashClaims() derive those claims from mutable totalAssetCash and totalfCash reserves relative to totalLiquidity, while the fCash component is discounted using the lagged oracleRate. A flash-loan-funded lend or borrow can atomically change the reserve composition. Although this manipulation only increases the token's unadjusted value, the risk-adjusted collateral value can fall because the fCash claim receives an additional fCash haircut while the asset-cash claim does not.
ground_truth.impact: An attacker can temporarily reduce a direct liquidity provider's risk-adjusted collateral value and cause an account near minimum collateralization to appear undercollateralized and become eligible for liquidation.
ground_truth.mitigation: Do not use current market reserves to determine liquidity-token collateral value. Use a manipulation-resistant TWAP to determine the liquidity token's collateral value.
ground_truth.title: [H-10] Liquidity token value can be manipulated

predictions.description: ExchangeRate.buildExchangeRate reads latestRoundData and checks only that the returned rate is positive. It does not validate updatedAt, answeredInRound, or round completeness. If the oracle is stale during an outage or delayed update, TradingAction's free-collateral and debt checks can use obsolete collateral valuations.
predictions.impact: Accounts may incur undercollateralized debt, or liquidators and users may receive materially incorrect settlement and liquidation prices, causing protocol losses.
predictions.mitigation: Require a nonzero updatedAt, enforce an acceptable maximum oracle age, validate answeredInRound against roundId where applicable, and reject incomplete or otherwise invalid rounds before using the price.
predictions.title: Stale Chainlink prices are accepted during collateral checks and trade settlement

predictions.description: Views.getCurrencyAndRates calls TokenHandler.getToken(currencyId, false) for both assetToken and underlyingToken. The second call should use the underlying=true selector, so callers receive the asset address in both fields.
predictions.impact: Integrations can approve or transfer the wrong token, causing failed operations or funds to be sent to an unintended token contract; systems that use the response for valuation can also mis-account collateral.
predictions.mitigation: Load underlyingToken with TokenHandler.getToken(currencyId, true), and add regression tests asserting distinct configured asset and underlying addresses for currencies that have both.
predictions.title: Currency rate view returns the asset token as the underlying token

predictions.description: AssetRate.getSupplyRate obtains a uint256 from the external AssetRateAdapter and then checks require(rate >= 0), which is always true for uint256. No upper bound or sanity range is applied before the value is used in rate calculations for idiosyncratic maturities.
predictions.impact: The protocol can calculate incorrect trade prices or become unable to execute trades, settle assets, or value positions for the affected currency; extreme values can also create denial of service through arithmetic failure.
predictions.mitigation: Define and enforce a governance-approved maximum annualized supply rate, reject values outside the supported protocol range, and validate adapter identity and returned rates before using them in market calculations.
predictions.title: Annualized supply-rate validation is ineffective and permits unbounded oracle output

predictions.description: transferFrom emits Transfer(from, to, amount) unconditionally after nTokenTransferFrom returns, without checking success. Because the interface explicitly returns a boolean, the backing proxy can report failure without reverting, while the adapter still publishes a successful-looking Transfer event.
predictions.impact: Off-chain accounting, payment processors, bridges, or monitoring systems that trust Transfer logs can credit recipients or record settlement for transfers that never occurred, causing accounting discrepancies or potentially financial loss.
predictions.mitigation: Only emit Transfer after confirming success; alternatively revert whenever the delegated call reports false. Ensure all callers and wrappers consistently treat unsuccessful delegated transfers as failed operations.
predictions.title: Transfer event is emitted even when delegated transfer fails

predictions.description: After transferFrom, the adapter emits Approval(msg.sender, from, newAllowance). The delegated allowance operation is for owner=from and spender=msg.sender, so the ERC20 Approval event arguments are reversed. This produces logs that do not describe the actual allowance state and can also be emitted for failed transfers.
predictions.impact: Wallets, routers, compliance systems, and indexers that rely on Approval logs can track the wrong allowance relationship, potentially approve or reject transfers incorrectly and create exploitable off-chain accounting or authorization decisions.
predictions.mitigation: Emit Approval(from, msg.sender, newAllowance) only when the delegated allowance mutation succeeds, and ensure event consumers use on-chain allowance state where correctness is security-critical.
predictions.title: Approval event uses reversed owner and spender fields

predictions.description: ExchangeRate consumes the oracle price while the available evidence does not show any use of the feed's decimals metadata or an explicit fixed-point normalization. If a configured feed uses a decimal precision different from the valuation convention, the raw answer is interpreted at the wrong scale.
predictions.impact: Collateral can be overvalued or undervalued by orders of magnitude, allowing excessive borrowing and insolvency or causing legitimate positions to be liquidated incorrectly.
predictions.mitigation: Define the required exchange-rate scale, read and validate the oracle's decimals or adapter metadata, normalize answers explicitly with checked arithmetic, and reject feeds whose precision or scale is incompatible with the valuation formula.
predictions.title: ExchangeRate may fail to normalize oracle decimals before collateral valuation

predictions.description: TokenHandler is the shared transfer primitive for balances, settlement, incentives, and token actions. If inbound accounting records the requested amount after transferFrom rather than measuring the recipient balance delta, fee-on-transfer, deflationary, or malicious ERC20 tokens can cause the protocol to credit more assets than it received.
predictions.impact: The protocol can become undercollateralized and attackers may withdraw assets or borrow against balances that were never received, creating direct losses for the protocol or depositors.
predictions.mitigation: For inbound transfers, measure the recipient balance before and after transferFrom and credit only the actual received amount, or explicitly restrict currency listings to tokens with exact-transfer behavior and enforce that invariant during governance configuration.
predictions.title: Nominal ERC20 transfer amounts may be credited without validating actual tokens received

predictions.description: AssetRate validation is described as checking only that the externally returned exchange rate is positive. There is no visible upper bound, deviation check, or sanity validation before the rate is used by settlement and collateral valuation. A manipulated or malfunctioning AssetRateAdapter or external cash market can therefore return an extreme but positive rate that the protocol accepts.
predictions.impact: An inflated rate can overvalue collateral or settled assets and allow undercollateralized borrowing or excessive redemption; a severely deflated or extreme rate can misvalue user positions, trigger unjustified liquidations, or cause arithmetic reverts that disrupt settlement.
predictions.mitigation: Validate the returned rate against configured bounds, expected decimal scale, prior-rate deviation limits, and any available underlying-market invariants. Reject abnormal values and pause or fall back safely when the rate exceeds those limits; ensure downstream arithmetic cannot overflow on accepted rates.
predictions.title: AssetRate accepts economically implausible positive exchange rates

predictions.description: The CompoundToNotionalV2 integration exposes owner-only token approval functionality, but the architecture provides no evidence that changing or removing an approval first revokes allowances granted to prior spenders. If an old spender is compromised, deprecated, or misconfigured, it may retain permission to transfer tokens subsequently held by the adapter.
predictions.impact: A former or compromised spender can drain ERC20 assets held by CompoundToNotionalV2, including tokens received during later operations, causing direct protocol or user fund loss.
predictions.mitigation: When changing an approved spender, first set the previous spender's allowance to zero and verify the operation before granting the new allowance. Prefer immutable, allowlisted spenders, exact per-operation approvals, and explicit revoke functions; use safe-approval handling for tokens that require zero-before-nonzero updates.
predictions.title: Previous token approvals remain active after Compound adapter approval changes

ground_truth.description: AuctionEscapeHatch._calculateMaltRequiredForExit() obtains Malt's current market price from UniswapHandler.maltMarketPrice(), which derives the price directly from the Uniswap pool reserves. exitEarly() uses the calculated Malt quantity to mint Malt, sell it for collateral, and transfer the output to the exiting user. A flash loan can manipulate the reserves and therefore the spot price used for this early-exit settlement.
ground_truth.impact: An attacker can manipulate the Uniswap spot price during an early exit and extract funds from the protocol.
ground_truth.mitigation: Use a TWAP oracle to track Malt's price instead of the current Uniswap reserve ratio.
ground_truth.title: [M-22] `_calculateMaltRequiredForExit` Uses Spot Price To Calculate Malt Quantity In `exitEarly`

predictions.description: UniswapHandler.buyMalt() passes amountOutMin = 0 to swapExactTokensForTokens(), so the caller accepts any amount of Malt returned by the router. Because the trade size is the entire reward-token balance, a searcher can sandwich the transaction and force an arbitrarily poor execution price.
predictions.impact: The protocol can spend substantially more reward tokens than intended for the acquired Malt, transferring value to sandwich attackers and reducing stabilization funds.
predictions.mitigation: Require a nonzero minimum output derived from a trusted price limit and bounded slippage, or use a deadline and explicit min-output parameter supplied by the protected caller. Apply equivalent protections to the sell path.
predictions.title: Uniswap buy path accepts zero minimum output

predictions.description: MaltDataLab.trackReserveRatio() is public and samples reserveRatio() from the Uniswap pool before updating the moving average. An attacker can temporarily manipulate pool reserves within a transaction or around the sampling call, invoke trackReserveRatio(), and leave the manipulated value as the moving average's latest sample.
predictions.impact: Liquidity-deficit calculations, stabilization decisions, auction behavior, and collateral valuation can be driven by an attacker-selected reserve ratio, enabling unfavorable trades or misdirected protocol funds.
predictions.mitigation: Restrict sampling to authorized keepers or a controller, enforce minimum time between observations, reject implausible deviations, and use a manipulation-resistant oracle or TWAP whose observation cannot be changed atomically with the sampled trade.
predictions.title: Permissionless reserve-ratio sampling enables flash manipulation of the moving average

predictions.description: UniswapV2Library.pairFor derives the pair address from a hardcoded init-code hash rather than querying the configured factory. If the configured factory deploys pairs with a different creation bytecode, or if the factory is misconfigured, reserve reads and quote calculations target an incorrect address. Calls to that address can revert or return invalid pricing data, disrupting liquidity and stabilization operations.
predictions.impact: Liquidity management, collateral-deficit calculations, and trade sizing can revert or operate on incorrect reserves, potentially halting stabilization and making dependent operations unavailable.
predictions.mitigation: Use the factory's pair lookup as the authoritative address, or validate at initialization that the configured factory's pair matches the derived address and reject incompatible factories. Verify pair existence before consuming reserves.
predictions.title: Hardcoded Pair Init Code Hash Can Route Reserve Reads to a Nonexistent or Wrong Pair

predictions.description: Reserve pricing and collateral calculations exponentiate and multiply by values derived from external token decimals, including 10**rewardDecimals, 10**maltDecimals, 10**collateralDecimals, and products of those scaled reserves. There is no visible upper-bound validation on decimal metadata or checked handling for oversized scaling factors. A token with unusually large decimals, or a misconfigured token, can make these operations overflow and revert whenever pricing or collateral status is queried.
predictions.impact: Reserve-dependent views and state-changing stabilization or liquidity operations that rely on them can become permanently unavailable, preventing collateral assessment, liquidity actions, and automated stabilization.
predictions.mitigation: Validate token decimals against a safe maximum during initialization/configuration, use bounded scaling with explicit overflow checks, and reject unsupported decimal combinations before enabling reserve-dependent operations.
predictions.title: External Token Decimal Metadata Can Cause Arithmetic Reverts in Reserve Pricing and Deficit Calculations

predictions.description: buyMalt records purchased as the handler's entire Malt balance after the swap rather than measuring the balance increase caused by the current trade. Any Malt already held by UniswapHandler—including tokens accidentally transferred there or retained due to an interrupted accounting flow—is sent to msg.sender along with the newly purchased amount. A caller possessing BUYER_ROLE can therefore capture unrelated Malt inventory.
predictions.impact: Unrelated Malt held by UniswapHandler can be transferred to the buyer, causing direct token loss and reducing funds available for stabilization or liquidity operations.
predictions.mitigation: Record the Malt balance before the swap, compute the post-swap increase, and transfer only that delta. Separately account for or reject pre-existing Malt inventory, and ensure BUYER_ROLE is assigned only to the intended stabilization contract.
predictions.title: buyMalt Sweeps Pre-existing Malt Balance to the Buyer

predictions.description: _distributeRewards approves the auction for the full rewarded amount before calling allocateArbRewards(), but the approval is not reset after the call. If allocateArbRewards consumes less than the approved amount, the auction retains an allowance to transfer reward tokens from StabilizerNode later.
predictions.impact: Reward tokens held by StabilizerNode can be drained up to the residual allowance, including tokens received after the original allocation.
predictions.mitigation: Use an exact-transfer pattern that sets allowance to zero after allocation, or approve only the amount actually consumed. Prefer safeIncreaseAllowance/safeDecreaseAllowance where appropriate and verify the auction spent exactly the intended amount.
predictions.title: Residual RewardToken Allowance Remains Authorized to Auction

predictions.description: MovingAverage exposes administrator-controlled sample parameters, but the available implementation facts do not indicate validation that sampleLength is nonzero. Setting the length to zero can make circular-buffer indexing or average calculation divide/modulo by zero, causing update and read operations to revert. Since MaltDataLab depends on MovingAverage for price samples, downstream oracle consumers may receive stale data or stabilization operations may halt.
predictions.impact: Moving-average updates can stop and downstream pricing, auction, liquidity, or stabilization logic can operate on stale data or become unavailable, potentially preventing protocol recovery actions.
predictions.mitigation: Require sampleLength > 0 and enforce a sane maximum in every configuration setter; reject invalid values before storing them. Add defensive checks in update and average functions so invalid configuration cannot cause protocol-wide reverts, and use a timelocked governance change for parameter updates.
predictions.title: Zero Sample Length Can Permanently Revert Moving-Average Updates

predictions.description: MiningService forwards Bonding callbacks to every configured reward mine. Because the mine list is administrator-managed and callback failures are not shown to be isolated, any configured mine that reverts can cause the entire MiningService callback to revert, propagating into Bonding operations such as stake, unstake, or balance updates.
predictions.impact: Users may be unable to bond, unbond, or update staking balances, potentially freezing staking and reward-accounting operations until the faulty mine is removed or configuration is repaired.
predictions.mitigation: Use bounded callback dispatch with per-mine failure isolation where safe, provide an emergency pause/removal mechanism, validate mine contracts before registration, and ensure Bonding operations cannot be permanently blocked by one reward mine.
predictions.title: Registered Reward Mine Revert Can Denial-of-Service Bonding Operations

predictions.description: The reinvestment flow withdraws rewards into RewardReinvestor and then performs the reward-to-Malt conversion before staking the result for a supplied account. If the swap amount is derived from the contract-wide reward-token balance rather than the balance delta produced by that withdrawal, any residual or unsolicited reward tokens held by the contract are included and credited to the account selected by the caller. A caller can invoke reinvest for their own account and capture rewards left over from a prior operation or transferred to the contract.
predictions.impact: Reward tokens belonging to other users or accidentally retained by the contract can be converted and credited to an attacker, causing direct loss of rewards and incorrect account balances.
predictions.mitigation: Record the reward-token balance before withdrawal, calculate the post-withdrawal delta, and swap only that delta. Ensure the staking beneficiary is bound to the account whose rewards were withdrawn, and separately handle or explicitly sweep residual tokens under a restricted administrative process.
predictions.title: RewardReinvestor Can Attribute Pre-existing Reward Balance to an Arbitrary Account

ground_truth.description: VaderPoolV2.burn() redeems an LP position against the pool's current reserves and passes the released asset amounts together with the position's original deposits to VaderMath.calculateLoss(). Because the reserves can be manipulated before liquidity removal, an LP can create an artificial impermanent loss value. VaderRouterV2.removeLiquidity() then submits the resulting coveredLoss to the reserve for reimbursement.
ground_truth.impact: An LP can receive VADER compensation for artificially engineered impermanent loss. With a sufficiently large LP position, the reserve payout can exceed the manipulation costs and allow profitable extraction of reserve funds.
ground_truth.mitigation: Use a manipulation-resistant oracle, such as a TWAP, for the relative prices of the pool's assets when calculating impermanent loss.
ground_truth.title: [H-06] LPs of VaderPoolV2 can manipulate pool reserves to extract funds from the reserve.

predictions.description: Both legacy and V2 router addLiquidity overloads accept amountAMin and amountBMin but explicitly discard them and invoke pool minting without enforcing minimum deposits or minimum liquidity. A searcher can front-run or otherwise change pool reserves before the transaction executes, causing the user to receive materially different liquidity than expected while the transaction still succeeds.
predictions.impact: Users can receive substantially fewer LP units or provide an unfavorable asset ratio, resulting in direct loss of deposited assets and value extraction by sandwichers.
predictions.mitigation: Calculate the actual deposited amounts and minted liquidity, then require each actual amount to meet its corresponding minimum and require minted liquidity to meet a caller-provided minimum; revert otherwise.
predictions.title: Liquidity add minimum amounts are ignored, enabling slippage and sandwich losses

predictions.description: VaderPoolV2.mintSynth is externally callable and its shown modifiers include nonReentrant and supportedToken but not onlyRouter. It calls nativeAsset.safeTransferFrom(from, address(this), nativeDeposit) using a caller-supplied from address, then mints synthetic tokens to a caller-supplied to address. Any attacker can therefore use a victim's native-asset allowance to the pool to transfer the victim's assets and direct the resulting synth tokens to the attacker.
predictions.impact: Approved users can have native assets drained from the pool allowance and converted into synth tokens sent to an attacker, causing direct loss of funds.
predictions.mitigation: Restrict mintSynth to the configured router and require from == the authenticated user where appropriate, or use msg.sender as the source and avoid arbitrary source addresses. Validate the recipient and add authorization tests covering unauthorized direct calls.
predictions.title: V2 mintSynth lacks router access control and can spend arbitrary approved users' native assets

predictions.description: When cycleTimestamp is expired, the mint logic sets cycleMints directly to uAmount without requiring uAmount <= dailyLimit. The same path is used for the first mint because cycleTimestamp is initially zero, allowing a caller authorized to trigger USDV minting to mint an arbitrary amount above the configured daily limit once per cycle.
predictions.impact: The intended daily USDV issuance cap can be exceeded by an amount of arbitrary size at the start of every 24-hour window, increasing USDV supply and potentially enabling excessive VADER conversion or draining backing liquidity.
predictions.mitigation: Require uAmount <= dailyLimit in the cycle-reset branch, or use a single accounting path that checks the resulting cycleMints value against dailyLimit before minting.
predictions.title: Daily mint limit is bypassed whenever a mint cycle rolls over

predictions.description: Both internal queue functions have empty bodies. _insertQueue therefore returns the default boolean value false without modifying the public queue mapping, while _executeQueue returns a zero reimbursement without processing any queued item. Any integration relying on this contract to enqueue or execute swaps will silently fail.
predictions.impact: Queued swaps can remain unprocessed indefinitely, causing denial of service for the queue functionality and potentially leaving assets or accounting state stranded in upstream integrations that assume successful queue execution.
predictions.mitigation: Implement and test linked-list insertion and execution, explicitly return success or revert on failure, validate queue invariants, and add tests proving that queued items are recorded, processed exactly once, and reimbursed according to the intended policy.
predictions.title: Swap queue operations are unimplemented and silently return default values

predictions.description: executeQueue reimburses msg.sender with the value returned by _executeQueue, but the current _executeQueue implementation returns the default value zero. The contract also exposes no withdrawal or recovery function. ETH forcibly sent to the contract cannot be recovered through the available interface.
predictions.impact: ETH held by the contract can become permanently inaccessible, and keepers or executors receive no reimbursement, preventing reliable operation of any intended queue maintenance process.
predictions.mitigation: Implement the reimbursement calculation and account for the contract balance explicitly; add a narrowly controlled emergency ETH recovery function protected by the intended governance or owner mechanism, and reject or safely handle unsupported funding paths.
predictions.title: Execution reimbursement is always zero and forced ETH cannot be recovered

predictions.description: XVader prices shares from the contract's current VADER balance. If deposits calculate newly minted shares from that balance without virtual shares, a holder can make a small initial deposit, directly transfer or otherwise donate a large amount of VADER to XVader, and cause a victim's subsequent deposit to mint zero or severely underpriced shares. The attacker can then redeem the initial shares for the victim-funded VADER.
predictions.impact: Victim deposits can be partially or wholly captured by the attacker, causing direct loss of VADER and dilution of depositor ownership.
predictions.mitigation: Use internal accounted assets rather than raw token balance for pricing, add virtual shares/assets or equivalent minimum-share protections, reject deposits that mint zero shares, and test direct-donation and first-depositor scenarios.
predictions.title: XVader share-price donation attack enables zero-share deposits

predictions.description: LiquidityBasedTWAP depends on Chainlink USD feeds but the available component evidence does not show validation of the feed round, update timestamp, answeredInRound, or positive answer before using the result. A stale, incomplete, or negative feed response can therefore be treated as a valid asset price by downstream reserve and USDV calculations.
predictions.impact: Users may mint or burn USDV at an incorrect exchange rate, allowing extraction of protocol assets or causing under-collateralized USDV and reserve accounting losses.
predictions.mitigation: Require positive answers, nonzero timestamps, complete rounds, and an explicit maximum age before accepting Chainlink data; revert or use a separately validated fallback when the feed is stale or invalid.
predictions.title: LiquidityBasedTWAP accepts stale or invalid Chainlink responses

predictions.description: VaderPoolV2 performs reserve-based swap and liquidity calculations across externally supplied ERC-20 assets, but the architecture provides no indication that it measures the actual balance received after transferFrom. A supported token that burns or diverts tokens during transfer can cause the pool to credit the requested amount rather than the amount received, making internal reserves and LP/synth accounting inconsistent.
predictions.impact: The pool can become undercollateralized, allowing attackers to extract valuable assets or causing LP holders and synth holders to suffer losses when the accounting discrepancy is realized.
predictions.mitigation: Either reject fee-on-transfer, rebasing, and callback-capable assets when configuring supported tokens, or calculate credited amounts from actual balance deltas and use those deltas consistently in reserve, LP, and synth accounting.
predictions.title: V2 pool accounting is vulnerable to fee-on-transfer or deflationary supported tokens

predictions.description: RewardsDistributionRecipient permits the owner to set rewardsDistribution to the zero address without validation. Once set, the onlyRewardsDistribution gate can no longer be satisfied by any external caller, preventing future reward notifications; if ownership is subsequently renounced or otherwise lost, the distributor cannot be repaired.
predictions.impact: Future rewards cannot be notified or scheduled, potentially stopping staking incentives and causing protocol reward operations to remain permanently disabled.
predictions.mitigation: Require the configured distributor address to be nonzero before assignment, emit an event for distributor changes, and use a recovery or two-step distributor update mechanism before ownership can be renounced.
predictions.title: Zero-address distributor assignment can permanently disable reward notifications

ground_truth.description: FlanBackstop.purchasePyroFlan() computes priceBefore and tiltedPrice directly from the instantaneous FLAN/stablecoin Uniswap pair balances. These values determine growth, flanToMint, and the premium ultimately minted to the caller as PyroFlan. An attacker can temporarily skew the pair balances with a flash loan or large trade and can split the operation into repeated smaller calls. The acceptableHighestPrice check only caps each observed tilted price and therefore does not make the spot inputs manipulation-resistant or stop a repeated attack within the configured limit.
ground_truth.impact: An attacker can manipulate the FLAN/stablecoin LP, especially when it is new or has low liquidity, to receive large amounts of PyroFlan backed by newly minted FLAN. By reducing the volume of each flash-loan attack and repeating it, the attacker can accumulate this gain while remaining below the per-call price ceiling.
ground_truth.mitigation: Use a TWAP instead of the pool price at a single point in time to increase the cost of a flash-loan sandwich attack.
ground_truth.title: [H-05] Flash loan price manipulation in purchasePyroFlan()

predictions.description: mint transfers the caller's base tokens, then computes proxy as the entire post-deposit baseToken balance divided by the pre-transfer redeem rate. It should calculate only the proxy value of the newly deposited amount. After an initial deposit establishes supply, a subsequent attacker can deposit a small amount and receive proxy tokens representing approximately the entire existing supply, inflating total proxy supply and allowing redemption of reserves belonging to earlier holders.
predictions.impact: Proxy token supply can be inflated and existing reserve backing can be drained, causing dilution and direct loss of base tokens for existing holders.
predictions.mitigation: Compute the proxy amount from the deposited amount using the pre-mint redeem rate, for example amount * ONE / _redeemRate, or otherwise calculate the change in reserve and update the rate and supply atomically. Add invariant and regression tests ensuring minted proxy value equals only the caller's deposit value.
predictions.title: Mint Calculates Proxy Tokens From Total Reserve Instead of Deposit Amount

predictions.description: redeem burns the caller's proxy tokens and invokes IERC20(baseToken).transfer(to, baseTokens) without checking the returned boolean or using a safe transfer wrapper. ERC20 implementations that return false instead of reverting can cause the proxy tokens to be burned while no base tokens are delivered.
predictions.impact: Users can permanently lose proxy tokens without receiving base tokens, and integrations may treat the redemption as successful.
predictions.mitigation: Use SafeERC20.safeTransfer, or require IERC20(baseToken).transfer(to, baseTokens) to return true, and ensure the payout failure reverts the entire transaction.
predictions.title: Redeem Ignores ERC20 Transfer Failure

predictions.description: Both functions declare returns (uint256) but never assign or explicitly return a value. Solidity therefore returns the default value zero even when tokens were minted or redeemed, creating an incorrect success result for callers that rely on the returned amount.
predictions.impact: Integrations can record zero assets for successful operations, mis-account balances, or fail to credit users after tokens have been transferred or burned.
predictions.mitigation: Explicitly return the minted proxy amount from mint and the redeemed base-token amount from redeem, and verify all callers use the returned values consistently.
predictions.title: Mint and Redeem Return Zero Despite Declared Return Values

ground_truth.description: NonUSTStrategy.investedAssets() converts the strategy's UST exposure into the vault's underlying asset using Curve's current get_dy_underlying() quote. Vault.totalUnderlying() includes that result, and deposit and withdrawal share calculations use totalUnderlyingMinusSponsored(). An attacker can temporarily move the Curve pool with a flash loan, make the same UST position appear to be worth more or less underlying, and deposit or withdraw while the vault uses that transient exchange rate.
ground_truth.impact: An attacker can mint too many vault shares or withdraw more underlying than their fair share at the expense of existing depositors.
ground_truth.mitigation: Value the UST exposure with a manipulation-resistant oracle or sufficiently long TWAP instead of Curve's transaction-local quote.
ground_truth.title: [H-03] Vaults with non-UST underlying asset vulnerable to flash loan attack on curve pool

ground_truth.description: ERC4626Oracle.getPrice() values an ERC4626 vault share by calling previewRedeem() for a share amount and multiplying the returned assets by the oracle price of the underlying asset. previewRedeem() delegates to convertToAssets(), which derives the assets-per-share value from the vault's current totalAssets() and totalSupply. Because deposits, mints, withdrawals, and redemptions can change those spot accounting values within a transaction or block, an attacker can temporarily inflate or deflate the LP-token price returned by the oracle.
ground_truth.impact: An attacker can make an ERC4626 LP token appear substantially more or less valuable than the underlying asset warrants. This can increase the attacker's borrowing power beyond the intended collateral value or make another account's collateral appear insufficient and trigger premature liquidation.
ground_truth.mitigation: Avoid using previewRedeem function to calculate the price of the LP token of an ERC4626 vault. Consider implementing TWAP so that the price cannot be inflated or deflated within a single block/transaction or   within a short period of time.
ground_truth.title: M-10: ERC4626Oracle Vulnerable To Price Manipulation

predictions.description: getPrice and getEthPrice consume latestRoundData but ignore updatedAt, answeredInRound, and roundId. During a feed outage, stalled transmission, or incomplete round, an old price remains usable by OracleFacade and RiskEngine as current collateral and debt valuation.
predictions.impact: RiskEngine can approve undercollateralized borrowing or reject valid withdrawals based on obsolete prices, potentially causing protocol bad debt or preventing solvent users from withdrawing.
predictions.mitigation: Validate updatedAt against a configured maximum age, require updatedAt != 0, require answeredInRound >= roundId where applicable, and revert when the round is incomplete or stale. Apply equivalent checks to the ETH/USD feed.
predictions.title: Stale Chainlink rounds are accepted for collateral valuation

predictions.description: The implementation assumes token feed answers are scaled by 8 decimals and converts the raw token answer directly against the raw ETH/USD answer. It never queries or validates AggregatorV3Interface.decimals(), so feeds with differing decimal precision produce prices scaled by the precision difference.
predictions.impact: Collateral may be overvalued by orders of magnitude, allowing excessive borrowing and protocol bad debt; alternatively it may be undervalued and make collateral unusable.
predictions.mitigation: Read decimals() from both feeds and normalize answers to a common fixed-point scale before division, or enforce and verify an immutable expected decimal value for every configured feed during setFeed.
predictions.title: Feed decimal mismatch can arbitrarily mis-scale token prices

predictions.description: Only negative answers are rejected. A zero ETH/USD answer causes division by zero in getPrice, making every token price request through that ChainlinkOracle revert. A zero token answer returns zero and can make collateral valuation unusable; if a zero-producing or incorrectly configured feed is accepted, the oracle can be selectively disabled or misprice assets.
predictions.impact: A zero ETH price can cause protocol-wide denial of service for assets using this oracle, while a zero token price can distort health calculations and block withdrawals or operations involving that asset.
predictions.mitigation: Require both token and ETH answers to be greater than zero and revert with a dedicated invalid-answer error before any arithmetic or price use.
predictions.title: Zero answers can disable pricing or create zero-valued collateral

predictions.description: DefaultRateModel derives utilization directly from the caller-supplied liquidity value. LToken supplies the underlying token balance as liquidity, so an attacker can temporarily transfer or flash-borrow a large amount of the underlying into the LToken, call the public updateState function, and withdraw or repay the temporary liquidity afterward. The rate model then observes an artificially low utilization for the entire elapsed accrual interval.
predictions.impact: Borrowers can avoid a substantial portion of accrued interest, reducing lender yield and reserve accrual and potentially causing protocol-wide financial loss when large outstanding borrows exist.
predictions.mitigation: Do not base accrual on an unprotected instantaneous token balance. Use a liquidity measure that cannot be temporarily inflated for the accrual call, such as a stored or time-weighted liquidity value, and ensure state updates use a trusted pre-update accounting snapshot. Consider restricting or carefully sequencing balance-changing operations around interest accrual.
predictions.title: Spot liquidity can be flash-manipulated to suppress borrow interest

predictions.description: AccountFactory creates account proxies while accepting the proxy administrator as a caller-controlled argument. No factory-level validation or binding to the account owner is shown, so any caller can select an arbitrary administrator, including an attacker-controlled address or contract, when creating an account. If accounts are created on behalf of users or through integrations that do not independently verify this parameter, the selected administrator can upgrade the proxy implementation and replace account logic with malicious code.
predictions.impact: An attacker-controlled proxy administrator can drain assets held by affected account proxies, alter authorization checks, or permanently brick account functionality through a malicious implementation upgrade.
predictions.mitigation: Restrict account creation or bind the administrator to the authenticated account owner; reject zero and unsuitable administrator addresses; preferably derive the administrator from immutable trusted governance or the initialized owner rather than accepting an unconstrained caller-supplied value. Add tests proving that an untrusted caller cannot obtain upgrade authority over another user's account.
predictions.title: Caller-supplied proxy administrator permits unauthorized upgrade control

predictions.description: The AaveV3Controller is described as mapping supply and withdraw assets, but no validation is shown for Aave V3's onBehalfOf parameter on supply or to parameter on withdraw. If the controller forwards these fields without requiring them to equal the calling Account, an authorized or improperly exposed account-call path can deposit assets into another user's Aave position or withdraw the Account's supplied assets directly to an attacker-controlled address.
predictions.impact: Collateral or supplied assets held by an Account can be redirected to an arbitrary Aave beneficiary or recipient, causing direct loss of user funds and potentially leaving the Account with debt or reduced collateral backing.
predictions.mitigation: Decode and validate onBehalfOf for supply and to for withdraw, requiring each to equal the Account being operated on unless an explicitly approved destination model is intended. Add negative tests for third-party beneficiaries and recipients, and ensure ControllerFacade cannot bypass these checks.
predictions.title: Aave V3 supply and withdraw recipients are not constrained to the Account

predictions.description: The AaveV2Controller is annotated as allowing withdrawals unconditionally while mapping the asset to an aToken. If the controller facade relies on this validation before allowing an account call, a caller can submit withdrawals for assets or targets that are not explicitly authorized by the account's configured Aave V2 position.
predictions.impact: Unauthorized account assets may be withdrawn from Aave V2 positions, or calls may be routed to an unintended pool, causing direct loss of collateral and bypassing protocol integration restrictions.
predictions.mitigation: Require every withdrawal to validate the canonical Aave V2 pool, verify that the asset has a registered reserve and expected aToken mapping, and reject assets or targets not present in the configured allowlist.
predictions.title: Aave V2 withdrawals are accepted without sufficient authorization checks

predictions.description: ERC4626 withdraw and redeem operations contain both receiver and owner parameters. The available ERC4626Controller summary does not show checks binding owner to the Account and receiver to the Account or an authorized destination. An unrestricted owner/receiver pair can permit share withdrawals from an approved owner and redirect assets away from the Account.
predictions.impact: ERC4626 shares or the assets obtained by redeeming them can be drained or redirected, causing loss of collateral and bypassing intended account ownership controls.
predictions.mitigation: Require owner to be the executing Account unless a separately authorized allowance model is implemented, and restrict receiver to the Account or an explicitly approved destination. Validate the full calldata before forwarding the call.
predictions.title: ERC4626 withdrawal and redemption authorization may permit arbitrary owners and receivers

predictions.description: UniV3Controller is observed to validate the input token and parse the swap path, but there is no evidence that the recipient encoded in swap calldata is required to equal the calling Account or another approved destination. If the controller permits a caller to cause an Account to execute an approved swap, the caller can encode their own address as the recipient and redirect swap proceeds away from the Account.
predictions.impact: Managed-account funds can be exchanged and delivered directly to an attacker, resulting in loss of the account's input assets and any resulting swap proceeds.
predictions.mitigation: Decode every supported swap payload, including swaps nested in multicall, and require the recipient to be the executing Account or an explicitly approved protocol-controlled destination. Reject arbitrary recipient values and ensure all relevant swap selectors are covered.
predictions.title: Uniswap V3 swap recipient is not constrained to the managed account

predictions.description: UniV3Controller is observed to check the input token allowlist while parsing Uniswap V3 token paths. A multihop path can therefore contain an unapproved intermediate or final output token unless every token encoded in the path is validated. This allows approved assets to be exchanged into arbitrary or worthless tokens and can introduce assets that the risk engine and controller policy do not support.
predictions.impact: The Account may lose approved collateral in exchange for unsupported or worthless assets; the resulting asset may be unpriceable, excluded from risk controls, or cause downstream accounting and liquidation failures.
predictions.mitigation: Decode and validate every token address in every supported path, including all intermediate hops and the final output token, with correct direction handling for exact-input and exact-output swaps. Require each token to be explicitly approved and supported by the protocol's asset and oracle policy.
predictions.title: Only the input token is allowlisted, permitting unsupported output and intermediate assets

predictions.description: ATokenOracle delegates the price of an aToken's underlying asset back to OracleFacade. If the underlying asset is mapped to ATokenOracle directly or through a chain of configured oracle adapters that returns to the original asset, price resolution recurses without a cycle or depth guard. A RiskEngine valuation request can then exhaust gas and revert.
predictions.impact: Valuation-dependent protocol operations revert or become unusable for assets in the cycle, potentially blocking liquidations and withdrawals and causing denial of service for affected accounts.
predictions.mitigation: Track visited assets or enforce a maximum oracle-delegation depth across OracleFacade and adapters; reject configurations where an aToken's underlying resolves back to the same asset or adapter, and validate mappings before activation.
predictions.title: ATokenOracle permits recursive oracle cycles through underlying-asset resolution

predictions.description: UniV2LPOracle derives an LP price from pair reserve balances and underlying prices obtained from OracleFacade. If raw reserve amounts are combined without normalizing each token to a common decimal basis, pairs containing 6-, 8-, or other non-18-decimal assets receive materially incorrect LP valuations.
predictions.impact: Collateral can be overvalued by orders of magnitude, allowing an account to borrow more assets than the LP position supports and leaving protocol bad debt after liquidation.
predictions.mitigation: Read both underlying token decimals and normalize reserve quantities and oracle prices to a single fixed-point scale before calculating the LP value; add tests covering common 6/8/18-decimal pair combinations and reject unsupported decimal configurations.
predictions.title: UniV2 LP valuation may mis-scale reserves for tokens with different decimals

predictions.description: UniV2LPOracle obtains prices for both pair tokens through OracleFacade. If a pair token is itself mapped to a UniV2 LP oracle that eventually references the original pair, the recursive calls can cycle indefinitely until the transaction runs out of gas or reverts.
predictions.impact: Borrowing, withdrawals, liquidations, and health-factor checks involving the affected collateral can be permanently blocked, creating a denial of service and potentially preventing timely liquidations.
predictions.mitigation: Track visited assets during a pricing request and reject repeated nodes; enforce a strict maximum recursion depth and validate oracle registrations so an LP cannot directly or indirectly depend on itself.
predictions.title: Recursive UniV2 LP oracle mappings can cause valuation denial of service

predictions.description: BalancerController validates join/exit request structure and pool-token information but does not appear to constrain the sender and recipient fields embedded in Balancer Vault requests to the managed Account. If an untrusted caller can cause the Account to submit a validated request, the request can direct pool shares, withdrawn assets, or other proceeds to an attacker-controlled address.
predictions.impact: Managed-account assets or Balancer pool proceeds can be transferred to an arbitrary recipient, causing direct loss of user collateral or liquidity-provider positions.
predictions.mitigation: Require the Balancer request sender and recipient to equal the managed Account, or use controller-generated values that cannot be caller-supplied; reject requests containing arbitrary recipients before forwarding them to the Vault.
predictions.title: Balancer join and exit recipients are not constrained to the managed account

ground_truth.description: Balancer strategy vaults mint strategy tokens from a deposit using the pre-deposit BPT balance and global strategy-token supply, then convert strategy tokens back to BPT using the current total BPT balance and the unchanged global supply. A user can enter immediately before the permissionless reinvestReward operation adds reward BPT, so the user's newly minted strategy tokens participate in the reward distribution without any deposit-duration snapshot. The user can then redeem those tokens immediately and receive a disproportionate share of the newly reinvested BPT.
ground_truth.impact: Loss of assets for the users as their BPT gain (rewards) can be stolen.
ground_truth.mitigation: Use snapshot-based reward accounting so BPT gains are weighted by deposit duration, and prevent users from entering and exiting in the same transaction or block. As additional defenses, restrict reinvestReward to authorized Notional callers, charge fees to users who do not borrow from Notional, and submit reinvestment transactions privately to reduce front-running.
ground_truth.title: [M-7] Gain From Balancer Vaults Can Be Stolen

predictions.description: The constructor stores the supplied lending pool, aToken, and underlying addresses independently, obtains decimals from the supplied underlying, and does not verify that the aToken belongs to that underlying or that the lending pool has a reserve for it. A deployment or governance configuration using mismatched addresses causes the aggregator to report the normalized income of one reserve as the exchange rate of another token.
predictions.impact: Balances can be materially overvalued or undervalued, allowing incorrect minting, redemption, collateral accounting, or protocol losses when users transact against the misconfigured asset.
predictions.mitigation: During construction, verify the aToken's underlying asset against the configured underlying, verify the lending pool's reserve configuration and aToken address for that underlying, reject zero or inconsistent addresses, and use an immutable trusted deployment registry where possible.
predictions.title: Unvalidated Aave asset configuration can create an incorrect exchange-rate oracle

ground_truth.description: UniswapV3OracleWrapper.getOnchainPositionData() reads the pool's current price, but getTokenPrice() does not use that value. Instead, getTokenPrice() derives a square-root price from the protocol's token oracles and passes it to LiquidityAmounts.getAmountsForLiquidity(), then sums the resulting token amounts and pending fees at those oracle prices. The wrapper does not require a pool whitelist or a minimum TVL before valuing the position. An attacker can create a low-liquidity pool whose position is primarily theirs, deposit that position as collateral, borrow against the reported value, and swap the pool so the position's actual token composition no longer supports the collateral value.
ground_truth.impact: An attacker can use a self-created low-TVL Uniswap V3 position as overvalued collateral, borrow from Paraspace, and then alter the position's pool composition so its realizable value falls below the outstanding debt, leaving the Lending Pool with a loss.
ground_truth.mitigation: Only allow Uniswap V3 positions from whitelisted pools that satisfy a sufficiently high TVL threshold before accepting them as collateral.
ground_truth.title: [H-05] Attacker can manipulate low TVL Uniswap V3 pool to borrow and swap to make Lending Pool in loss

predictions.description: NFTFloorOracle permits an administrator to update NFT floor prices without the validation applied to ordinary role-gated updates. An administrator account that is compromised, misconfigured, or malicious can publish an arbitrary inflated floor price, which the pool may use for collateral valuation and borrowing decisions.
predictions.impact: The attacker can obtain undercollateralized loans or prevent liquidation, potentially causing protocol bad debt and loss of lender funds.
predictions.mitigation: Require administrator updates to pass the same validation as all other updates, including nonzero and bounded prices, maximum deviation from the previous value, and freshness constraints. Use a timelocked or multisignature governance path for exceptional changes, and emit update events suitable for monitoring.
predictions.title: Administrator Can Bypass NFT Price Validation

predictions.description: The supply path can be vulnerable if it mints pTokens or updates reserve liquidity using the user-supplied nominal amount after calling ERC20 transferFrom, without measuring the actual balance increase. A fee-on-transfer or deflationary asset would deliver fewer tokens than the amount credited, allowing the supplier to receive excess pool shares and potentially withdraw assets supplied by other users.
predictions.impact: The reserve can become undercollateralized and lose assets belonging to other depositors; repeated exploitation can drain the affected reserve.
predictions.mitigation: Either restrict reserve listings to standard ERC20s with no transfer fees, or measure the reserve balance before and after transferFrom and use the actual received amount consistently for reserve accounting, interest-rate updates, and share minting. Reject transfers whose received amount does not match the expected amount if exact-amount semantics are required.
predictions.title: Supply Accounting May Overmint Shares for Fee-on-Transfer ERC20 Assets

ground_truth.description: StakingModule.stakedByAt() reads an account's stake history through CheckpointsUpgradeable.getAtBlock(). When an account stakes and exits in the same block, the checkpoint history can contain both the large stake and the zeroed post-exit value for that block. The historical lookup can then return the earlier same-block stake value, causing balanceOfAt() to expose an incorrect historical balance even though the account no longer retains the corresponding stake.
ground_truth.impact: A same-block stake and exit can cause balanceOfAt() to report an incorrect historical stake. In this repository, the value is exposed through a standalone view and the slashing path uses the latest stake value instead. The direct consequence is inaccurate historical stake reporting; further loss requires a downstream integration that relies on this view.
ground_truth.mitigation: Require an account's exit to occur at least one block after the block in which the original stake was created, so a stake cannot be opened and closed within the same checkpoint block.
ground_truth.title: H-1: Flashloan `TEL` tokens to stake and exit in the same block can fake a huge amount of stake with minimal material cost

predictions.description: addPlugin accepts any address without checking that it is a contract implementing the IPlugin interface. A zero address, EOA, or reverting/malicious contract can therefore enter the plugin array. Staking, exits, claims, and views iterate over the array and invoke plugin methods, while stake and exit paths unconditionally invoke notifyStakeChange.
predictions.impact: Users may be unable to stake, exit, claim, or query balances until the bad plugin is removed; sufficiently large plugin registries can also make operations exceed the block gas limit.
predictions.mitigation: Require nonzero contract code and validate the expected interface before registration; enforce a bounded plugin count; invoke notifyStakeChange only when requiresNotification returns true; consider isolating callback failures so one plugin cannot halt core staking operations.
predictions.title: Unvalidated plugin registration enables global denial of service

predictions.description: removePlugin deletes a plugin from the registry but does not migrate, claim, or otherwise expose its outstanding liabilities. SimplePlugin.claim is restricted to the StakingModule, so after removal users cannot claim balances held by that plugin through the module, and the removed plugin's liabilities are excluded from aggregate claimable and totalSupply calculations.
predictions.impact: Outstanding TEL rewards can become inaccessible indefinitely, while displayed total supply and claimable balances underreport the system's liabilities.
predictions.mitigation: Require a migration or settlement procedure before removal, keep removed plugins claimable until all liabilities are zero, and maintain removed-plugin claim routing or an explicit recovery mechanism for affected users.
predictions.title: Removing a plugin can permanently strand user rewards

predictions.description: _stake increases the user's checkpoint and _totalStaked by the requested amount before calling safeTransferFrom, but never verifies the module's balance increase. If the configured TEL token charges transfer fees, burns tokens, or otherwise transfers less than requested, the module credits more stake than it holds.
predictions.impact: Early withdrawers can drain available TEL, leaving later stakers unable to exit; rescue logic also treats the inflated _totalStaked as the protected liability and cannot repair the deficit.
predictions.mitigation: Restrict TEL to a known standard token or measure the balance before and after transferFrom and credit only the amount actually received; validate the configured token during initialization.
predictions.title: Stake accounting can exceed actual TEL received for fee-on-transfer or nonstandard TEL

predictions.description: FeeBuyback.submit calculates the referral reward using _telcoin.balanceOf(address(this)) rather than the TEL received from the current transfer or swap. Any TEL already held by FeeBuyback, including residual funds from prior operations or unsolicited transfers, is approved and credited to the supplied recipient. A legitimate owner submission can therefore misallocate unrelated funds, and a compromised or malicious owner can direct the entire residual balance to an arbitrary recipient.
predictions.impact: Unrelated TEL held by FeeBuyback can be assigned as referral rewards to an arbitrary account, causing permanent misallocation or theft of residual fee funds and inflating that account's claimable balance.
predictions.mitigation: Record the TEL balance immediately before the transfer or swap, calculate the positive balance delta afterward, and credit only that delta. Validate the swap output and use SafeERC20 for all token transfers and approvals; isolate or reject unsolicited and residual balances.
predictions.title: FeeBuyback credits all residual TEL balance to the current referral

predictions.description: FeeBuyback.submit invokes IERC20.transferFrom and IERC20.approve directly without checking their boolean return values or using SafeERC20. Tokens that return false instead of reverting can make the funding or approval step fail silently, while execution continues to the aggregator and referral credit path.
predictions.impact: FeeBuyback can process an operation without receiving the declared input or granting the intended allowance, while still potentially assigning existing TEL as referral rewards; this can create incorrect rewards and loss of contract-held funds.
predictions.mitigation: Replace raw transferFrom, transfer, and approve calls with SafeERC20.safeTransferFrom and forceApprove/safeApprove as appropriate. Revert whenever funding or allowance setup fails, and credit only measured balance deltas after successful operations.
predictions.title: FeeBuyback ignores ERC20 transfer and approval return values

predictions.description: claimAndExitFor accepts independent account and to parameters and performs both _claim(account, to, auxData) and _exit(account, to) without requiring authorization from the affected account or validating that to is the account or an approved migration destination. Any holder of RECOVERY_ROLE can therefore invoke the paused migration path for a victim account and direct the victim’s staked principal and claimable rewards to an attacker-controlled address.
predictions.impact: All migrated stake and pending rewards of targeted users can be permanently transferred away, causing direct loss of user principal and earned TEL.
predictions.mitigation: Require a user-signed migration authorization binding account, destination, nonce, and migration parameters, or restrict to to == account or an approved migration contract. Add replay protection and emit events containing the authorized destination and migration nonce.
predictions.title: RECOVERY_ROLE can redirect users’ migrated principal and rewards to an arbitrary recipient

vulnerable_code.function: claimAndExitFor(address account, address to, bytes calldata auxData)

predictions.description: FeeBuyback.submit accepts an unrestricted wallet address and arbitrary walletData, then executes wallet.call from the FeeBuyback contract before performing any other validation. A compromised or malicious owner can use this primitive to invoke token transfers, approvals, or arbitrary contract methods with FeeBuyback as msg.sender, bypassing the narrower intended swap workflow.
predictions.impact: FeeBuyback-held ERC20 or native assets can be transferred to an attacker, and allowances or downstream contract state can be modified, causing loss of fee-rewards funds.
predictions.mitigation: Replace the generic wallet.call with narrowly specified operations or enforce an immutable/administrative allowlist of wallet targets and permitted function selectors; validate calldata and prohibit calls that transfer FeeBuyback assets or modify arbitrary allowances.
predictions.title: Owner-controlled arbitrary call enables FeeBuyback asset and approval exfiltration

predictions.description: After transferring the source token from the safe and calling the external aggregator, submit only checks the low-level call success flag. It does not verify that the aggregator produced any TEL, that the TEL balance increased by an expected minimum, or that the source amount was actually consumed. A successful no-op, underperforming, or compromised aggregator call is therefore treated as a completed referral swap.
predictions.impact: Fee tokens can be removed from the safe without delivering the corresponding TEL referral reward; the referral recipient receives an incorrect or zero credit while the source assets remain with or are consumed by the aggregator.
predictions.mitigation: Record the TEL balance before the swap, require the post-swap increase to meet a caller-supplied or configured minimum output, and validate that the source token transfer and aggregator execution satisfy the expected amount and route.
predictions.title: Successful aggregator call is accepted without verifying TEL output

ground_truth.description: BLVaultLido allows an owner to deposit and withdraw around an external oracle update without a minimum holding period. On withdrawal it caps returned wstETH using only the current oracle price, while the Balancer exit executes against the pool state. An attacker can deposit while the pool matches the pre-update oracle, move the pool toward the known post-update price, wait for the oracle update, and then withdraw. Because the withdrawal check now uses the updated oracle, the vault returns the full manipulated wstETH amount instead of capturing the arbitrage for the Treasury.
ground_truth.impact: An attacker can repeatedly sandwich predictable oracle updates to extract value from the vault, causing recurring losses to remaining vault liquidity.
ground_truth.mitigation: Lock the user into the vault for a minimum amount of time (i.e. 24 hours).
ground_truth.title: H-1: Adversary can sandwich oracle updates to exploit vault

predictions.description: BLVaultManagerLido derives mint and withdrawal valuations from Chainlink OHM/ETH and stETH/ETH feeds. The loaded implementation exposes configurable update thresholds, but the supplied code does not demonstrate validation of answer positivity, round completeness, timestamp freshness, or answeredInRound consistency before prices are used. If any of these checks are absent, a stale or invalid feed response can determine the OHM amount minted or the wstETH amount returned.
predictions.impact: Vault users or the protocol can receive materially mispriced OHM or wstETH, enabling undercollateralized OHM minting, excess redemptions, or treasury losses.
predictions.mitigation: For every feed response, require answer > 0, updatedAt != 0, answeredInRound >= roundId, and updatedAt within a bounded nonzero freshness interval. Enforce safe minimum and maximum threshold values and fail closed when validation fails.
predictions.title: Oracle pricing can accept stale or otherwise invalid Chainlink data

predictions.description: BLVaultLido.getOutstandingRewards and _sendRewards iterate over auraRewardPool().extraRewardsLength() and make external calls for every configured extra reward pool. The vault does not impose a local maximum on the number of pools or a bounded processing mechanism. If the configured Aura reward pool contains sufficiently many entries, or one entry becomes reverting or excessively expensive, claimRewards and withdrawals with claim_=true can run out of gas or revert persistently.
predictions.impact: Users can be unable to claim accumulated rewards and may be unable to complete withdrawals that request reward claims; accumulated rewards can remain trapped in the vault until the external configuration is repaired.
predictions.mitigation: Bound the number of processed extra reward pools, maintain an allowlisted and capped reward-token configuration, and provide paginated or independently callable reward-claim processing so a single bad or expensive pool cannot block withdrawals or all claims.
predictions.title: Unbounded Aura extra-reward processing can block reward claims and withdrawals

ground_truth.description: CurveOracle.getPrice() retrieves the price of each underlying token in a Curve LP pool, selects the minimum price, and multiplies it by the LP token's virtual price to calculate its USD value. If the price of one or more underlying tokens is manipulated, the minimum-price calculation can be skewed and produce an incorrect USD value for the LP token. An attacker can exploit this incorrect valuation to profit at the expense of other users.
ground_truth.impact: An attacker can manipulate the price used to value Curve LP tokens and profit at the expense of other users. Exploitation can result in significant financial losses for affected users.
ground_truth.mitigation: Use TWAP prices for the Curve pool's underlying assets.
ground_truth.title: H-4: Potential flash loan attack vulnerability in `getPrice` function of CurveOracle

predictions.description: _approve calls approve(spender, 0) and approve(spender, amount) directly and ignores both return values. Tokens that return false without reverting can leave the allowance unset while execution continues to Paraswap, causing a failed or inconsistent swap; nonstandard approval behavior is not safely handled.
predictions.impact: Swaps can fail or become unavailable for affected assets, potentially blocking withdrawals, liquidations, or strategy operations; integrations that do not atomically revert all surrounding state may also experience inconsistent execution.
predictions.mitigation: Use OpenZeppelin SafeERC20.safeApprove or safeIncreaseAllowance-compatible logic, and explicitly handle tokens requiring zero-before-nonzero approval. Restrict supported assets if token behavior cannot be normalized.
predictions.title: ERC20 approval return values are ignored

predictions.description: UsingBaseOracle stores the constructor-supplied IBaseOracle without checking that it is nonzero or a deployed contract.
